html:
Builders and general contractors in Greer ZIP 29650 usually call us at the same point: the trades are almost done, the buyer or inspector is coming, and there is a layer of dust over a house that otherwise looks finished. Homeowners finishing a kitchen or bathroom renovation call at the same point, just with more patience. Either way, post construction cleaning in Greer is not a bigger version of house cleaning. It is a different job, with different tools, and a different order.

Who we clean for in 29650

ZIP 29650 sits in Greer, close to I-85, SC-14, SC-101 and US-29, and a lot of Upstate growth has landed here, from additions on older homes to new builds near GSP Airport and the BMW plant. The jobs we see fall into four types:

  • Homeowners finishing a remodel or addition
  • Builders and general contractors handing over a new home
  • New construction closings with a firm date
  • Kitchen and bathroom renovations in occupied homes

What is included

The list is long on purpose. Construction dust is fine enough to get inside drawers and light fixtures, so we clean those areas, not just visible surfaces.

AreaWhat gets done
Surfaces and trimFine dust removed from ledges, trim and all flat surfaces
Cabinets and closetsInside drawers, cabinets and closet shelves
WindowsGlass, tracks and sills, with paint specks and stickers removed
FixturesLight fixtures, vents and ceiling fans
BathroomsNew fixtures polished, tile and glass cleaned
FloorsVacuumed and washed with multiple passes
FinalA touch-up pass before move-in

How much does post construction cleaning cost in Greer?

Builders tend to ask this with a square-foot rate in mind, but the honest answer is that two homes of the same size can take very different time. Drywall sanding creates the most fine dust, so a house with heavy finishing takes longer. The number of windows with residue, the number of rooms affected, and whether you book the rough clean, final clean and touch-up together all play a role. A tight closing or inspection date may call for a larger crew.

Perfect Services gives a price only after a free in-home estimate. A team member visits the site, looks at the dust and the scope and gives you a price with no commitment. Book it through the form on the Greer post-construction page, call (864) 399-5168 or text (864) 666-8520.

The three-stage idea, in plain words

Think of the clean as stages that follow the construction schedule. The rough clean happens after the heavy work, the final clean after the last painter and trim carpenter, and the touch-up right before the buyer walks in. Booking all three means fewer surprises, because each visit starts from a house that is already mostly clean. Our post-construction cleaning service page explains the stages for contractors.

What a rushed clean misses

We have walked into houses where the floors were mopped but the tops of the doors were still white with dust. Walk your own job and run a finger over these spots: the top edge of door frames, inside the bottom drawer of the kitchen, the inside of the range hood, window tracks, and the inside lip of the bathroom vanity. If any of them leave a gray line on your finger, the house needs another pass.

Timing

Small renovations take a long day. A full new build is a multi-day, multi-person job. Booking this week is possible depending on the calendar, but contractors should call early because the final clean is almost always tied to a deadline.

Before we arrive

  1. Have the crew remove trash, scrap and packaging.
  2. Make sure water and power are on.
  3. Tell us if there are protective films on counters or floors that should stay.
  4. Point out any surfaces that are delicate, such as unsealed stone.

If the project is outside the 29650 area, we also work in Lyman and nearby towns. For another look at what each trade leaves behind, read post-construction cleaning before the holidays in Greer. Not sure whether you need this service or a deep clean? Start with the estimate request and describe the project.

Homeowners versus builders

The two groups need different things. A builder wants speed and consistency across several houses, a reliable team that shows up on the day the buyer is coming, and a result that reads the same house after house. A homeowner living through a remodel usually wants something gentler: someone who understands that the family has been eating off paper plates for six weeks and just wants the kitchen to feel like a kitchen again.

For homeowners, we recommend deciding in advance which rooms you will use first. Cleaning the kitchen and a bathroom well, then the bedrooms, lets you move back in gradually while the rest of the house is finished. For builders, it helps to send the closing date and a list of the houses at the start of the week so the crew can be planned.

Surfaces that need a careful hand

New does not mean tough. Freshly installed stone, unsealed grout, brushed metal fixtures and new hardwood can all be marked by the wrong product or too much water. We ask about the finish of each surface at the visit, and we use the gentlest method that works. If a surface has not cured yet, such as freshly sealed floors, the team will tell you to wait rather than risk it.

When the last trade leaves, book your free estimate for post-construction cleaning in Greer.
faqs: What is the difference between post-construction cleaning and a deep clean?
Post-construction cleaning removes fine dust, paint specks, adhesive and stickers from new work and uses multiple floor passes. A deep clean targets built-up household dirt.
